heroHeadline: PLA 12 Sorties (9 Cross Median Line) on May 10; Lai Warns HIMARS Deadline (May 31) at Risk From KMT Budget Constraint; US C-17s Land in Beijing; 4 Days to Trump-Xi Summit
heroSubtitle: PLA posted 12 sorties on May 10, 2026 — 9 of 12 crossing the median line into northern and southwestern ADIZ sectors, with 5 PLAN vessels and 1 official ship — re-escalating from 8 sorties on May 9. The May pre-summit sortie sequence stands at: 4 (May 1) → 29 record (May 2) → 1 (May 3) → 2 (May 4) → 1 (May 5) → 0 (May 6) → 22 (May 7) → 12 (May 8) → 8 (May 9) → 12 (May 10). Four days remain before President Trump travels to Beijing for the May 14-15 summit with Xi Jinping, where US C-17 transport aircraft have already begun landing for pre-summit logistics. Secretary of State Rubio confirmed Taiwan will be on the agenda. On May 9, President Lai Ching-te warned that Taiwan may miss the NT$800 million HIMARS down payment deadline (May 31) because the KMT-inserted procedural constraint in the NT$780B Special Defense Budget — passed 59-0 on May 8 — requires the Executive Yuan to submit LOA reports and obtain legislative approval before funds can be disbursed. If the deadline lapses, the HIMARS procurement case must be restarted. The US State Department responded bluntly: 'Funding delays can only benefit Beijing.' CFR and CSIS pre-summit analyses warn Beijing will press Trump on limiting future US arms sales to Taiwan, opposing Taiwan independence, and blocking senior US official visits to Taipei. Taiwan Deputy FM Francois Wu's warning — 'What we are most afraid of is to put Taiwan on the menu of the talk between Xi Jinping and President Trump' — remains the defining phrase of the pre-summit diplomatic atmosphere. The $14B PAC-3 MSE/NASAMS package remains on hold pending summit outcome.
